sentences.text: The holotype fossil represents a juvenile individual measuring less than one meter in length and weighing approximately two kilograms.
This small dinosaur possessed very long arms, a well-developed wishbone, and likely bore feathers due to its evolutionary position within the group Paraves.
Its long hindlimbs suggest it was capable of fast running, while research suggests it may have possessed opposable front claws.
The specimen had a brain volume of 14 cubic centimeters, representing the largest brain-to-body size ratio of any discovered dinosaur.
The species name feinbergi honors the Feinberg family, who acquired the specimen, and references the Disney character Bambi.
The excavation of the holotype skeleton yielded approximately 95 percent completeness, making it an exceptionally well-preserved find.
A 14-year-old named Wes Linster discovered the Bambiraptor skeleton in 1993 near Glacier National Park in Montana.
Bambiraptor feinbergi was named and described in 2000 by David Burnham, Kraig Derstler, Phil Currie, Robert Bakker, Zhou Zhonge, and John Ostrom.
The holotype specimen is currently housed in the American Museum of Natural History in New York.
Research suggests Bambiraptor may have had opposable first and third fingers allowing it to place food in its mouth.
David A. Burnham hypothesized that Bambiraptor may have been arboreal based on its enlarged cerebellum.
An alternative hypothesis suggests the large brain evolved to hunt agile prey such as lizards and mammals.
Bambiraptor is classified within the family Dromaeosauridae and is placed in the subfamily Saurornitholestinae.
Bambiraptor lived about 72 million years ago in Montana during the Late Cretaceous, specifically between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
It is debated whether Bambiraptor is a distinct genus or merely a juvenile Saurornitholestes, though some believe it should be synonymized with that species.
Some researchers suspect the holotype specimen is a chimera because it contains elements from three different similarly sized lower legs.
Published phylogenetic analyses have placed Bambiraptor far from Saurornitholestes, contradicting the idea that it is simply a young version of that genus.
